## 1 Epidemiological highlights

• Epidemiological situation : No new health zone affected.
The cumulative total remains at 48 health zones affected out of 140 in the five provinces, of which 47 remain in active transmission.

• Trend of cases : Over the past 24 hours, 98 new confirmed cases, 50 confirmed deaths and 14 recoveries were recorded :

o Ituri : 87 new confirmed cases were notified, mainly in Bunia (28), Mongbwalu (22), Rwampara (17), Kilo (5), Lita (4), Mandima (3), Nizi (3), Nia-Nia (2), Komanda (1), Mahagi (1) and Tchomia (1), 31 deaths among which, 51,6% community.

o Nord-Kivu : 11 new confirmed cases were reported (Butembo 2, Katwa 5, Beni 2 and Musienene 2) as well as 19 deaths (after harmonisation with the health zones, see table 2), including 5 community.
The provincial cumulative total reaches 325 confirmed cases and 223 deaths, representing a case fatality rate of 68,6%.

o Haut-Uélé : No new confirmed case or death was reported.
The provincial cumulative total remains at 39 confirmed cases and 21 deaths, representing a case fatality rate of 53,8 %, distributed across 5 health zones out of 13 in the province.

o Sud-Kivu and Tshopo : No new confirmed case or death was reported.
The cumulative totals remain respectively at 5 cases, 4 deaths, 1 recovered for Tshopo and 3 confirmed cases including 1 death and 2 recovered in Sud-Kivu.
The health zone of Miti-Murhesa reaches a total of 62 days whilst the province of Tshopo has 13 days without a new confirmed case.

• Analysis : Ituri remains the epicentre of the outbreak, concentrating 88,9 % of cumulative cases and 88,8 % of the new confirmations of the day.
Contact tracing performance remains insufficient and requires a strengthening of surveillance activities.

## EPIDEMIOLOGICAL AND OPERATIONAL CONTEXT

Declared on 15 May 2026, the 17th outbreak of Ebola virus disease (MVE) due to Bundibugyo ebolavirus continues its course within a complex humanitarian and security context.
Initially confined to the health zone of Mongbwalu (Ituri), it spread to five provinces (Ituri, Nord-Kivu, Sud-Kivu, Haut-Uélé and Tshopo), now affecting 48 health zones.
Population movements, insecurity, artisanal mining activities and cross-border trade with Uganda and South Sudan continue to promote transmission.
Multisectoral coordination remains mobilised in order to strengthen surveillance, intensify response interventions and limit the spread of the outbreak.

[FIGURE: Figure 1 — Chronology of events of the Ebola-Bundibugyo virus disease outbreak]

### 2.3 Mapping of confirmed cases

The spatial distribution confirms transmission mainly concentrated in Ituri, notably in the health zones of Bunia, Rwampara, Mongbwalu, Nizi, Lita and Nyankunde, with transmission continuing in already affected zones, including the health zone of Rungu in Haut-Uélé.

[FIGURE: FIGURE 2 — SPATIAL DISTRIBUTION OF HEALTH ZONES HAVING REPORTED CONFIRMED CASES]

The continuation of transmission in the health zone of Rungu in Haut-Uélé bears witness to the continuation of transmission in already affected zones, underlining the need to maintain simultaneously intensive interventions at the epicentre level and preparedness activities in neighbouring provinces.

### 2.4 Temporal analysis — epidemic curves

The epidemic curve shows sustained transmission during weeks W25 to W30, with fluctuations linked to notification delays and the progressive consolidation of data.

[FIGURE: FIGURE 3 — EPIDEMIC CURVE BY WEEK OF NOTIFICATION]

[FIGURE: FIGURE 4 EPIDEMIC CURVE BY DATE OF ONSET OF SYMPTOMS (DHIS2 LINE LIST)]

The outbreak remains in a phase of sustained transmission, with a high level of virus circulation.
Recent fluctuations must be interpreted with caution due to notification delays and the progressive consolidation of data.

### 2.5 Demographic characteristics

The age pyramid shows a predominance of working-age adults (18–50 years).
Minors under 18 years and elderly persons over 50 years are proportionally less affected.

[FIGURE: FIGURE 5 — CONFIRMED CASES BY SEX AND AGE GROUP]

[FIGURE: FIGURE 6 — DEATHS BY SEX AND AGE GROUP (AMONG CONFIRMED CASES)]

The distribution of cases by sex remains balanced.
The predominance of cases among working-age adults reflects more frequent community and occupational exposures, whilst the proportion of paediatric cases bears witness to the persistence of intrafamilial transmission.

In total, 1 425 alerts (including 1 263 new), 1 142 investigated within 24h (80,1%) and 321 validated (213 live and 108 community deaths).
This improvement reflects the reduction of investigation carry-overs and the consolidation of data originating from the affected provinces.
The improvement in the investigation rate is linked to the reduction of investigation carry-overs and the strengthening of surveillance teams in the affected provinces.

### 3.2 Laboratory : testing and positivity

→ Ituri : 206 samples documented in the collection network, including 87 positive (71 live and 16 deaths), representing an apparent positivity of 42,2 %.

→ Nord-Kivu : 100 samples received and analysed, among which 11 positive (6 live and 5 deaths), representing a positivity of 11,0%.

→ Haut-Uélé : No sample received and analysed to date.

→ Tshopo : 3 samples received and analysed.
All these samples came back negative after analysis.

In total, 733 patients were in isolation, including 313 confirmed cases and 420 suspect cases, representing an overall bed occupancy rate of 77,3 % (733 patients for 949 beds), for 859 admissions and 126 discharges (14 recovered, 22 deaths, 85 non-cases and 5 escaped).
Ituri concentrates the bulk of the burden with 544 patients in isolation (290 confirmed, 254 suspects) for 808 beds, representing 67,3% occupancy.
In Nord-Kivu, 189 patients are in isolation (23 confirmed, 166 suspects) representing an occupancy rate of 134,0 % (141 beds).
Haut-Uele and Tshopo did not make data available at the time of compilation.

## 7 Response activities by pillar

COORDINATION
Holding of the coordination meeting with the various partners ; Monitoring of field activities

CONTINUITY OF ESSENTIAL HEALTH SERVICES (CSSE)
→ Ituri : Continuation of the estimation of PCI (PCI — infection prevention and control) input needs in the framework of continuity of essential services and care ; Analysis of indicators drawn from DHIS2 (in progress) ; Development and Budgeting of the CSSE pillar plan.

LOGISTICS
→ Ituri : 38 vehicles and 11 Ambulances (PNC, HGR (HGR — general referral hospital) Bunia and 9 ZS) were made available to the various pillars to ensure the transfer of cases and the mobility of pillars in the field).

→ Nord-Kivu : Handover of 2 ambulances to the ZS of Beni for MVE response activities ; Delivery of inputs to the INRB laboratory ; Data collection and Drafting of section reports ; Reception of SDB inputs from partner FHI 369 ; Delivery of nutritional care inputs to the ZS of Beni : (250 boxes) and ZS of Mutwanga (200) ; Reception of the 2nd batch of nutritional care inputs (2411 boxes of plumpy nut, 11 boxes of F100 and 14 boxes of F75 and PCI inputs destined for the ZS of Butembo, Katwa and Beni/donation from UGPDSS

PCI / WASH
→ Nord-Kivu : Decontamination of 3/31 Households of Confirmed cases including 2 in Katwa and 1 in Butembo ; Decontamination of 10 ESS of stay of cases including 2 in Butembo, 6 in Katwa and 2 in Musienene ; Provision of incomplete PCI kit in 5 ESS in Butembo ; PCI score card assessment in 1 ESS in Butembo with an average score of 22,5% (CS Vutike) ; Follow-up and support of 141 ESS including : 20 in Beni, 32 in Butembo, 7 in Katwa, 4 in Kyondo, 2 in Musienene and 76 in Oicha ; Briefing of 490 ESS providers during supportive supervisions including : 60 in Beni, 113 in Butembo, 35 in Katwa, 23 in Kyondo and 259 in Oicha ; Community deaths having benefited from an SDB : 43 including 6 in Beni, 14 in Butembo, 21 in Katwa, 5 in Kyondo and 2 in Musienene ; Community deaths having been subject to SWAB : 54 including 11 in Beni, 1 in Butembo, 25 in Katwa, 5 in Kyondo, 2 in Musienene

→ Tshopo : Poor waste management, Insufficiency of receptacles, Triage service not functional, Personnel not trained in PCI and Insufficiency of dustbins.

COMMUNICATION (RCCE / CREC)
→ Ituri : 2088 people were reached by awareness messages delivered by RECO (RECO — community health worker) 54 in households of 1 out of 4 Health Zones (NIA-NIA, NIZI); 256 people were reached on awareness themes during educational talks held by community actors in health zone (NIA-NIA, NIZI).

→ Nord-Kivu : Support to the case management pillar ; Discharge ceremony of a military recovered patient at CTE-Beni : on this occasion, messages were delivered to other military personnel, to representatives of motorcycle taxi drivers present and to the community who came for a guided tour of the CTE.

→ Tshopo : 15 868 people were reached during awareness activities.
(ZS Mangobo, Kabondo, Tshopo, Lubunga and Makioso Kisangani) ; people were reached during door-to-door awareness at bloc meteo and and sotraco in the town of Kisangani.

→ Haut-Uélé : Briefing with CREC teams of the ZS of Isiro with a view to intensifying CREC interventions in the affected AS (AS — health area) ; visit of 27 Recos to households aimed at passing messages on the importance of SDB to heads of households.

HOLISTIC CASE MANAGEMENT (PECH)
→ Ituri : 13 new recovered ; 544 patients in isolation, 92 new admissions and 86 discharges including 19 deaths ; 988 people benefited from hot meals ; Reception of biochemistry equipment (High flow and Picollo + Accessories) at CTE Rwampara in Ituri.

→ Nord-Kivu : Discharge of a military recovered patient at CTE Beni.

→ Tshopo : No new admission ; 2 non-cases discharged and no patient hospitalised.
Continuation of experimental treatment of 2 contacts (D10) at CS FEDI of Mangobo.

RESEARCH, INNOVATION & VACCINATION
→ Ituri : Detection of gaps, halting the spread of the BDBV virus outbreak : protocol validated and preparation for launching surveys (Support Africa CDC) ; Study of the dynamics of interprovincial and cross-border spread from the epicentre : causes : Uncontrolled movements of patients and lifeless bodies, many uncontrolled border points, corruption at intra- and interprovincial checkpoints.

SAFE AND DIGNIFIED BURIALS (EDS)
→ Ituri : Conclusion of training of the 2 teams (Niania and pk 51) ; D2 of training of the 2 SDB teams in the ZS of Fataki, AS Jina ; Continuation of training of the two teams in Kasenyi : D3 ; Start of training of the 2 ECUMER teams in AS MWANGA and KUNDA in the ZS of RWAMPARA ; Reception of 10 boxes of water by the SDB pillar thanks to support from FHI 360.

→ Nord-Kivu : 37 SDB performed, 39 Bodies Swabbed and secured out of 42 alerts reported escorting during the burial of a confirmed case at the cemetery of Paida ; a disturbance of public order occurring during the burial was contained by security forces

PREVENTION OF SEXUAL EXPLOITATION AND ABUSE (PSEA / PRSEAH)
→ Ituri : 107 Participants (55 Women and 52 Men) bringing to a cumulative total of 2 597 people including 1482 Men and 1115 women already briefed and having signed codes of conduct in 5 Health zones of Ituri (Bunia, Rwampara, Mongbwalu, Lita and Aru) and revitalisation of the 12 CBCM in Mongbwalu ; 153 Participants (80 W/G and 73 M/B) bringing to a cumulative total of 15 329 people including 7 995 Men/boys and 7 334 women/girls sensitised in the Health zones of Bunia, Rwampara, Aru and Munbgwalu.

## 8 Main challenges, impacts and actions required


| N° | Challenges | Impact | Actions required |
|---|---|---|---|
| 1 | Reluctance to post-mortem sampling (SDB/swabs), community resistance and insecurity targeting SDB teams (attack at Muchanga bridge, paralysis of activities in Nyankunde) | Confirmation delay, underestimation of cases, disruption of key activities | Intensify CREC, involve religious and community leaders, secure teams, increase the number of SDB teams |
| 2 | Non-payment of providers (strike in the ZS of Bunia and Rwampara ; resumption announced after intervention by the military governor of Ituri) | Interruption of response activities, including safe and dignified burials | Regularise payment of providers ; secure dedicated funding |
| 3 | Insufficient CTE/CT capacity : occupancy of 134,0 % in Nord-Kivu (bed capacity : 141) and 67,3 % in Ituri (544 patients for 808 beds) ; | Admission delays, increased risk of nosocomial transmission | Accelerate construction and expansion of CTE, deploy temporary facilities, systematically report bed capacity |
| 4 | Low contact tracing performance in Ituri 77,6% ; Nord-Kivu 82,6% and Haut-Uele 60,0 | Chains of transmission not interrupted | Train, deploy and motivate community relays (RECO) ; reinforced supervision ; investigate the observed drop in Ituri |
| 5 | Insufficient ambulances and prepositioning at PoC | Delays in transfer and isolation | Preposition ambulances (including at PoE/PoC), deploy CT by ZS |
| 6 | Insufficient supply of MEG and medical inputs | Weakening of overall care | Advocacy and urgent supply of essential medicines |
| 7 | Insufficiency of PCI inputs (PPE, chlorine) and limited functional triage units (175/1 170, or 15 %) | High risk of nosocomial infections (123 PPL cases including 37 deaths in Ituri and 11 PPL including 3 deaths in Nord-Kivu) | Urgent supply, strengthening of PCI training |
| 8 | Geographic extension (Haut-Uélé, Tshopo) and high mobility | Risk of urban, river and cross-border diffusion | Activate the 23 priority PoE/PoC in Haut-Uélé ; strengthen cross-border coordination |
| 9 | Installation of local laboratories (Butembo and Mambasa) | Long confirmation delays, undetected transmission | Accelerate the deployment of decentralised diagnostic capacities |
| 10 | Insufficient financial resources | Limitation of pillar implementation | Urgent resource mobilisation, advocacy with partners |
| 11 | Insecurity and limited access (CODECO, ADF) | Restriction of operations | Strengthening of security coordination and humanitarian access |
| 12 | Continuity of essential services (CEHS) compromised | Increase in indirect mortality (non-Ebola) | Effective implementation of free healthcare, strengthening of CEHS |
